stem: A headteacher models the number of children who bring a ‘healthy’ packed lunch to school on any day by the distribution $\text{B}(150, p)$. In the past, she has found that $p = \frac{1}{3}$. Following the opening of a fast food outlet near the school, she wishes to test, at the 1% significance level, whether the value of $p$ has decreased.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: State the null and alternative hypotheses for this test.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.stem: On a randomly chosen day she notes the number, $N$, of children who bring a ‘healthy’ packed lunch to school. She finds that $N = 36$ and then, assuming that the null hypothesis is true, she calculates that $\text{P}(N \leqslant 36) = 0.0084$.
parts.text: State, with a reason, the conclusion that the headteacher should draw from the test.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: According to the model, what is the largest number of children who might bring a packed lunch to school?
